business.description: Rajputana Biodiesel Limited is one of India's emerging manufacturers of biodiesel with a strong presence in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The company operates an aggregate approved production capacity of 170 KLPD across two manufacturing facilities and is expanding into Compressed Biogas (CBG) with two approved units in Ajmer and Nagaur, Rajasthan, intending to emerge as a fully integrated bio-energy company across solid, liquid, and gaseous fuels.

outlook.statement: India's biodiesel market estimated at around Rs. 4,800 crore in FY 2025-26 and projected to expand further in FY 2026-27. Public sector OMCs issued procurement requirements of 60 crore litres during the year. CBG emerging as key component of India's clean fuel mix supported by SATAT framework, blending obligations in city gas network, and rising emphasis on converting agricultural and organic waste into usable energy. Biomass-based solutions gaining ground as industries seek alternatives to conventional solid fuels. Future belongs to integrated renewable energy companies participating across biodiesel, CBG, and allied bio-energy segments.

Focus will remain on building a resilient and integrated renewable energy platform capable of creating long-term value with responsibility. Opportunities ahead are significant but need to be pursued with prudence, clarity, and commitment. Leverage Verra-backed carbon credentials to deepen engagement with customers and investors who value measurable, verifiable sustainability outcomes. Maintain rigorous financial discipline ensuring each phase of expansion is supported by cash flows, risk management, and governance standards appropriate for a listed company.
Strengthen core biodiesel business through operational excellence, quality leadership and disciplined participation in institutional demand
Build out CBG platform with Rajputana Agro LLP as backbone for feedstock security and scaling in line with demand visibility
Develop thoughtful presence in biomass-based solid fuels where feedstock readiness, production capability, market acceptance and implementation feasibility align
India's biodiesel blending target of 5% by 2030 as per Inter-Ministerial Committee roadmap
Inter-Ministerial Committee constituted on 10th March 2026 to deliver comprehensive report and implementation plan within 6 months
CBG segment: 5,000+ CBG plants targeted nationally under SATAT ecosystem over time
PROM estimated domestic market opportunity of Rs 3,500 crore by 2030
We firmly believe that sustainability serves as a fundamental driver for long-term success, and we remain dedicated to playing our role in fostering a greener and more sustainable future.

India biodiesel market projected at about Rs 45,000 crore in FY 2026-27, up from Rs 40,000 crore in FY 2025-26; sector building steadily with room for expansion as procurement systems, OMC blending infrastructure, off-take mechanisms and feedstock linkages strengthen.
Medium-term case supported by cleaner-fuel adoption, waste-oil utilisation economics, circular-economy models, and policy continuity targeting 5% biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030.

High-level Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) formed to resolve long-term off-take solution based on feedstock-linked pricing rather than fixed mechanism; IMC to provide roadmap and policy interventions by September end to achieve 5% blending target by 2030.

The near-term outlook for the sector remains encouraging, supported by an improving policy framework, stronger demand creation mechanisms and expanding gas infrastructure across the country. These factors are collectively creating a stronger foundation for fresh investments and long-term project development.
Over the coming years, CBG has the potential to evolve into one of the most practical renewable fuels within the Indian context because it aligns naturally with the country's structural realities.

The outlook remains constructive because demand is no longer dependent only on voluntary green adoption. Industrial users are seeking reliable, lower-emission substitutes for coal, furnace oil and firewood, while power plants are being encouraged to co-fire biomass pellets with coal.
Our focus is to add value to these by-products, exploring the potential for exports in the bio-diesel segment.

During FY 2025–26, the Company has crossed the threshold limits specified under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, making CSR provisions applicable. Accordingly, the Company has constituted a CSR Committee responsible for formulating the CSR Policy, recommending CSR projects and expenditure, and monitoring implementation in line with Schedule VII of the Act. As the Committee was constituted during the current year and projects are under planning, no CSR expenditure has been incurred during FY 2025–26 and the CSR outlay will be spent in FY 2026–27 in compliance with statutory provisions.
